headline: On November 14, 2003: Astronomers discover Sedna
captionCards: Sedna's surface holds reddish tholins from methane-derived compounds
It remains one of the largest known dwarf planets without a moon
instagramCaption:
Sedna, a distant dwarf planet, was discovered in 2003.


It orbits far beyond Neptune, with a diameter of roughly 1,000 km. Its surface contains water, carbon dioxide, and ethane ices, plus reddish tholins from methane. Unlike most trans-Neptunian objects, it has no known moons. This lack of moons means its mass and density remain unknown.

Its discovery expanded understanding of the Solar System’s outer limits.
